homeGuide.title: Create a Graph TD diagram online
homeGuide.intro: Mermaid turns text into diagrams. Start with graph TD to arrange a flowchart from top to bottom, then describe the steps and arrows between them. This editor shows a live preview as you edit, with no account required.
homeGuide.step1: Paste your Mermaid code into the editor, or try the example alongside this guide.
homeGuide.step2: Change the labels, connect the nodes, and check the preview for syntax errors.
homeGuide.step3: Choose Export Drawing to download a PNG image or an SVG for your documentation.
homeGuide.exampleHeading: A decision flowchart you can edit
homeGuide.exampleCode:
graph TD
    A[Start] --> B{'{'}Ready?{'}'}
    B -->{'|'}Yes{'|'} C[Create diagram]
    B -->{'|'}No{'|'} D[Review requirements]
    D --> B
    C --> E[Export SVG or PNG]
homeGuide.replacesCode: Replaces the code currently in the editor.
homeGuide.syntaxHeading: Graph TD and flowchart TD: what is the difference?
homeGuide.syntaxOverview: Both graph TD and flowchart TD declare a top-down Mermaid flowchart. Use LR instead of TD for a left-to-right layout. In the example above, A[Start] creates a rectangular node, B{'{'}Ready?{'}'} creates a decision diamond, and -->{'|'}Yes{'|'} adds a labeled arrow.

docs.title: Mermaid Chart Documentation
docs.subtitle: Quickly learn how to create various diagrams using Mermaid syntax
docs.resourcesDesc: This page provides basic Mermaid syntax guidelines. For more advanced features and detailed syntax, please refer to:

flowchart.syntax1: defines a top-down graph (TD = Top Down)

sequence.syntax3: creates a solid arrow for synchronous messages
sequence.syntax4: creates a dashed arrow for return/asynchronous messages

class.syntax5: indicates B inherits from A (B is a subclass of A)

state.syntax2: represents the start or end state
state.syntax3: creates a transition from A to B

gantt.syntax5: defines a task, its start date, and its duration or end date

pie.syntax3: defines a slice of the pie chart

docs.quickStartDescription: Choose a diagram below, copy its plain-text source, and select Try in Editor to preview it. For flowcharts, graph TD and flowchart TD both create a top-down layout; graph LR runs from left to right. Use node IDs to connect steps and quotes around labels containing punctuation. Paste the source without Markdown code fences.
